contract: Production AI Engineering Proof Contract v1

experiments.claim: Before any change, the governed path allows the action, executes it once and attributes it to the version and rule that allowed it.
experiments.hypothesis: Under v1 the restart is allowed by a named rule, executed once, and the deploy system of record shows one restart.
experiments.invariant: Every executed action names the config version and rule that allowed it.
limitations: One agent, one action: the baseline the other proofs change.
experiments.question: Under v1, does the incident agent's production restart run, and is it attributed to v1?
experiments.setup: Bootstrap v1; the incident agent runs its fixed plan in a long-lived runtime process.
experiments.title: P1 · Baseline: the control plane allows

experiments.claim: Governed behaviour changes centrally while agent code, runtime process and request are held fixed.
experiments.hypothesis: The same request to the same process with the same agent code is ALLOW under v1 and APPROVAL_REQUIRED under v2, with no new side effect.
experiments.invariant: Agent sha256, runtime process and request hash are equal before and after; agent edits 0; redeploys 0.
limitations: P2 fails by design if code, process or request changes (control_plane_poc/tests/test_cheating.py).
experiments.question: Change only the control plane. Does the same process, with the same code and request, now stop for approval?
experiments.setup: Run the restart under v1; publish restart-requires-approval (v2) centrally; send the identical request to the same process.
experiments.title: P2 · One central change, same agent
experiments.variable: The control plane version (v1 → v2); nothing else.

experiments.claim: A held action waits for an eligible approver, executes once, and a duplicate resume is refused.
experiments.hypothesis: 0 restarts before approval, 1 after; ineligible approvers (the agent among them) refused; a second resume refused.
experiments.invariant: Exactly one execution, after an eligible approval.
limitations: Approvals are simulated principals, not a real identity provider.
experiments.question: Does the held action stay unexecuted until an eligible human approves, and then run exactly once?
experiments.setup: v2 holds production restarts for approval; the agent, an ineligible principal and an eligible approver act on the approval.
experiments.title: P3 · Approval, then exactly one execution
experiments.variable: Who approves, and how often the action is resumed.

experiments.claim: A central suspension takes effect at the next enforcement point of a run in flight, denies new runs, and leaves other agents alone.
experiments.hypothesis: 0 in-flight calls execute after the suspension; a new run is denied AGENT_SUSPENDED; the other agent keeps executing.
experiments.invariant: No call of the suspended agent executes after the suspension reaches its runtime.
limitations: Takes effect at the next enforcement point, not mid-call; a partitioned runtime is P9a.
experiments.question: Does a central suspension stop new runs and a run already in flight, and only that agent?
experiments.setup: Pause a run after two tool calls, publish a break-glass suspension, let the run continue; start a new run; run another agent.
experiments.title: P4 · Suspend: the kill switch

experiments.claim: Quotas and budgets set centrally are enforced per call and per run.
experiments.hypothesis: Call 3 is denied TOOL_CALL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; the run after the budget is spent is denied DAILY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.
experiments.invariant: No call beyond the quota; no run beyond the budget.
limitations: Spend is metered from simulated token counts and prices.
experiments.question: Does a central quota stop the third tool call, and an exhausted budget stop the next run?
experiments.setup: Publish max_tool_calls 2, then a daily budget below the spend so far.
experiments.title: P5 · Budgets and quotas

experiments.claim: One central revocation stops every agent that uses the server, and only those.
experiments.hypothesis: 0 calls reach the server after the revocation; the agents that use it are denied; the agent that does not is unaffected.
experiments.invariant: No call reaches a disabled server.
limitations: The MCP servers are simulated boundaries: this is central revocation, not MCP protocol interoperability.
experiments.question: Does disabling one server centrally stop every agent that uses it, and no other?
experiments.setup: Two agents use the observability server, one does not; publish the server as disabled.
experiments.title: P6 · Revoke one MCP server for every agent

experiments.claim: Agents name no model; the control plane chooses it by profile and data class, and fails closed when no model is cleared.
experiments.hypothesis: The default moves centrally; confidential data with no cleared model is denied rather than falling back.
experiments.invariant: No agent source names a model; no confidential call reaches an uncleared model.
experiments.question: Can the control plane move the default model and withdraw a model without an agent naming one?
experiments.setup: Publish a new default model (v2), then withdraw the only model cleared for confidential data (v3).
experiments.title: P7 · Model governance

experiments.claim: A governance change can be canaried, rolled back and promoted without touching agents.
experiments.hypothesis: Only part of the runs take the canary; after rollback none do; after promotion all do.
experiments.invariant: Bucketing is deterministic by run id; rollback leaves no run on the canary.
limitations: Buckets by run id hash; no real traffic shaping.
experiments.question: Does a canary reach only its bucket of runs, and does rollback return every run to the stable version?
experiments.setup: Roll v2 out to a percentage bucket of run ids; roll back; promote.
experiments.title: P8 · Staged rollout and rollback

experiments.claim: Without its control plane the runtime serves reads from last-known-good within a staleness bound, fails mutations closed, never applies a tampered bundle and makes no call without a credential.
experiments.hypothesis: Mutation denied CONTROL_PLANE_UNREACHABLE; everything denied past the bound; tampered bundle rejected; broker down denies calls.
experiments.invariant: No mutation without a fresh, verified policy and a credential.
limitations: A suspension cannot reach a partitioned runtime: exposure is bounded by the staleness bound and fail-closed mutations, not removed.
experiments.question: What does the runtime do without its control plane: for reads, mutations, stale policy, tampered bundles?
experiments.setup: Three scenarios: partition a runtime and publish a suspension it cannot see (P9a); alter a bundle in transit (P9b); stop the credential broker (P9c).
experiments.title: P9 · When the control plane is unreachable

experiments.claim: Comparing desired and observed state detects a silently stale runtime and the action it took under a superseded version.
experiments.hypothesis: rt-b reports v1 while v2 is desired; drift findings name it and its action; after reconcile no instance is stale.
experiments.invariant: Every instance reports its observed version; a mismatch is a finding.
limitations: Detection, not prevention: the stale runtime acted before it was detected.
experiments.question: Can the control plane see a runtime that is quietly running an old version, and what it did meanwhile?
experiments.setup: A lagging replica serves rt-b the old pointer without error while v2 is published.
experiments.title: P10 · Desired vs observed state

experiments.claim: Remove the control plane (embed governance in each agent) and the property P2 shows breaks: a change becomes a code edit that a running process does not see until it is redeployed.
experiments.hypothesis: Governed: 0 edits, 0 redeploys. Embedded: edits and redeploys, and the running process still restarts after the edit.
experiments.invariant: A governance change needs no agent edit and no redeploy, and applies at the next enforcement point.
limitations: Three agents; the edit and redeploy counts are for that estate.
experiments.question: Without a control plane, what does the same set of governance changes cost, and when do they take effect?
experiments.setup: The same four changes, applied once through the control plane (P11b) and once as edits to agents that embed governance (P11a).
experiments.title: P11 · Negative control: governance inside every agent

experiments.claim: Changes to the control plane are authorized by scope, need a second person to widen, may only restrict under break-glass, are validated, and are all on a tamper-evident local log under POC assumptions.
experiments.hypothesis: An agent and an out-of-scope lead are rejected; an in-scope lead restricting its own agent is accepted; widening alone, self-approval, break-glass widening and a plaintext credential are rejected; the chain verifies and breaks when one row is edited.
experiments.invariant: Every attempt is on the change log; only authorized, valid changes become signed versions.
limitations: Tamper-evident on one machine under the POC's assumptions; not an external immutable audit store. No MFA or real identity provider.
experiments.question: Who may change the control plane, and is every change, accepted or rejected, on the record?
experiments.setup: Ten attempts by agents, team leads, the platform admin and on-call, against config/admins.yaml.
experiments.title: P12 · Governing the control plane itself

experiments.claim: The evidence is internally consistent, recomputable from the raw state, and reproduced exactly by a rerun.
experiments.hypothesis: Every chain and signature verifies; no plaintext credential; no runtime restarted; one agent source hash; every request hash recomputes; the rerun differs only in masked process ids.
experiments.invariant: The evidence recomputes; the rerun is equivalent.
limitations: SHA256SUMS is a checksum list, not a signature. The signing key is a POC file, not a KMS.
experiments.question: Does the recorded evidence hold together: chains, signatures, credentials, processes, code and request hashes, and a rerun from source?
experiments.setup: Recompute from the raw state the scenarios left behind (tools/proof_facts.py); rerun every proof from source into a scratch copy (tools/verify_run.py --record).
experiments.title: Evidence integrity and replay
